title: Sensor steps explain the Hawaii (KIP) microseism rise; the 52-station GSN 14-20 s microseism rise continues to 2026, but its uncertainty is about 10 times the published value
abstract: Aster et al. (2023) reported that primary-microseism (14-20 s) energy at 52 Global Seismographic Network stations increased by 0.27 +/- 0.03 % per year (3 sigma) in 1988-2022. Their straight-line fits have no step terms at instrument changes. We used EarthScope MUSTANG daily PSD modes for all vertical broadband sensors, FDSN metadata epochs and co-located second sensors to measure steps at 257 primary-sensor breaks. Raw trends reproduce the published ones (r = 0.75, mean 0.29 % per year). A joint 24-month block bootstrap gives a 95 % interval of 0.06 to 0.51 for the 52-station mean, about 10 times wider than published. Co-located sensors resolve 74 breaks; steps at sensor model changes are biased positive (mean +0.088 dB, 18 of 24 positive). Correction lowers the mean to 0.22 (-0.03 to 0.45). With expected artifacts from unresolved breaks, instrument changes explain about 0.06-0.15 % per year, one quarter to one half of the published rate. With data to October 2026 the corrected mean is 0.26 (0.08 to 0.44), and the 2022-2026 data agree with the extrapolated trend. At KIP (Oahu), two positive steps (2006 gain change +0.40 dB, 2018 STS-6A +0.36 dB) cause most of the published increase: the corrected 1999-2025 trend is -5.4 % per decade, which agrees in sign with three Hawaii NDBC buoys (Hs^2 -4 to -9 % per decade). Limitations: 71 % of breaks are unresolved; MUSTANG modes are integer dB; a break-robust free-level estimate (0.01, -0.48 to 0.53) cannot separate zero from the published rate.

citations.reason: Source of the tested claim and of the station list and published trends; we find instrument steps explain part of the network trend, most of the KIP trend, and that the uncertainty is much larger; the network increase continues to 2026.
The step-corrected KIP microseism record agrees in sign with the NDBC Hawaii wave decrease that this study reported and asked to confirm independently.
